title: Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification
Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification
summary: The paper addresses efficient text classification, where deep neural models achieve strong accuracy but are slow to train and test. It proposes fastText, a linear model with a rank constraint, bag-of-words/n-gram features, hierarchical softmax, and asynchronous SGD on CPUs. On sentiment and tag-prediction benchmarks fastText is on par with deep-learning classifiers while being orders of magnitude faster; the target AG News test accuracy with h=10 and bigrams is 92.5%.

def get_engine():

    except ImportError:

        ("fasttext-wheel", "fasttext-wheel 0.9.2 = prebuilt wheel of facebookresearch/fastText v0.9.2 (authors' C++ trainer + official Python binding)"),
        ("fasttext", "fasttext PyPI source build of facebookresearch/fastText (authors' code)"),
    ]:

Pipeline: (1) AG News from the Zhang et al. 2015 release (found in REPRO_DATA_CACHE, verified 120,000 train / 7,600 test, balanced 4 classes), normalized with a byte-faithful Python port of the authors' classification-results.sh normalize_text pipeline; (2) learning rate selected from the paper's grid {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5} on a dedupe-grouped 10% validation holdout carved from the train split (12,026 lines, zero content-hash overlap with the 107,974-line search-train split), averaged over 3 seeds; (3) final model trained on the full 120k train split with the paper's config (dim h=10, wordNgrams=2, epoch=5, minCount=1, bucket=10M as in the authors' script, 20 threads) and evaluated on the untouched official test split over 5 seeds. Result C1: 92.27% ± 0.16 test accuracy (paper: 92.5%); C2 (no bigrams): 91.29% ± 0.03 (paper: 91.5%) — both within ~0.25 points of the paper's Table 1 values. All numbers computed by code; no paper values embedded. The lr search ran twice (lr=0.25 and lr=0.5 were selected on different runs; they are statistically tied on validation accuracy, ~92.1% each) and both choices reproduce the target within tolerance. results/metrics.json contains the full config, per-seed values, lr-search log, data checks, engine provenance, and repo git hash.

tolerance.why: AG News test accuracy is a percentage on a large fixed test set, and the paper reports no confidence interval. A 1.0 absolute band covers normal run-to-run variation, one-decimal rounding, and the undisclosed learning-rate choice from the paper's small validation grid.

audit_summary: The reproduction uses the authors' own fastText C++ trainer (fasttext-wheel 0.9.2, same upstream v0.9.2 source the paper's CLI uses) on the correct Zhang et al. AG News splits (120,000 train / 7,600 test), with the paper's exact h=10, bigrams, 5-epoch configuration, a validation-selected lr from the paper's grid, 20 CPU threads, and the official test split kept untouched (validation is a dedupe-grouped 10% carve-out of train, zero content overlap). The clean re-run is consistent with the logged run (C1 = 92.38 +/- 0.11 over 5 seeds, C2 = 91.24), i.e. within the 1.0-point tolerance of the paper's 92.5/91.5, and the ~1 s/epoch timing matches the paper's own speed claim, which argues against any fabricated numbers. No paper result values appear in the code, all reported values are computed by training, and the runtime is far too short and self-consistent to be hard-coded. Disclosed deviations are bucket=10M (authors' script) instead of the paper's 100M for unigram+bigram and flat softmax instead of the hierarchical Huffman softmax; neither cheapens the objective for the 4-class AG News task, though hierarchical softmax (R4) and the 100M-bin setting (R8) are strictly not implemented. Extra seeds beyond the paper are added repeats, not a scale-down; nothing about the target value's run was reduced. The remaining ~0.12-point gap is explained by hogwild-SGD run-to-run noise plus the paper's unspecified lr value, validation split, and tokenization.

requirement_check.evidence: prepare_data.py applies the authors' classification-results.sh normalize_text to the Zhang et al. release; C1 trains with wordNgrams=2 (word unigrams + adjacent bigrams) on the 120k train / 7.6k test splits (data/provenance.json: 120000/7600, balanced 4 classes).

Model is the authors' unmodified fastText C++ supervised trainer (fasttext-wheel 0.9.2); its architecture is exactly the average-of-embeddings lookup A followed by linear B and softmax, with dim=10 for both text representation and embeddings (A2).
loss='softmax' in reproduce.py/config.py minimizes the negative log-likelihood over the 4 classes; the objective is the paper's -1/N sum y_n log f(BAx_n).

Hierarchical softmax over a Huffman tree is NOT used; the run uses the flat softmax (fastText's default and the authors' script default), a deviation disclosed in metrics.json 'notes'. For k=4 the two only differ in normalization cost and are numerically near-equivalent, so the reported AG News accuracy is not a cheapened approximation of the objective, but the Huffman-tree trick itself was not exercised.

thread=20, fastText hogwild asynchronous SGD with its default linearly decaying learning rate (lrUpdateRate); clean re-run shows ~1 s/epoch per seed, consistent with the paper's CPU setting and Table 2.

dim=10, epoch=5, lr selected on a held-out validation split from {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5}; selected_config.json logs the full grid (means 91.05 / 91.91 / 92.11 / 92.12, argmax lr=0.5) averaged over 3 seeds.

Only AG News was run, so 'same parameters for all sentiment datasets' cannot be verified; the config is a single shared constant block and the two reproduced rows (C1 bigrams, C2 no bigrams) use identical hyperparameters apart from wordNgrams.

bucket=10,000,000 was used even though the configuration has unigrams+bigrams; the paper's Section 2.2 says 10M 'if we only used bigrams, and 100M otherwise'. The implementer justifies this by the authors' own script and a ~4 GB memory limit and discloses it in metrics.json; the hashing trick itself is used.
